judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The element is a div with role="link" (class imagem-destaque) in the "Nossas histórias" section; it is not focusable (no href, no tabindex), and the theme script makes it navigate on mouse click through data-is-link="/institucional/nossas-historias". Its only child is a figure holding an aria-hidden img and a figcaption whose span reads "Conheça a história da Emily". claimTrue: the CDP accessibility node captured from Chromium has role link and name "" (no nameFrom), so the sentence that the browser exposes a link and computes no name holds for the capture; the clause that a screen reader announces only "link" is overstated, since the caption text is an exposed descendant that browse mode reads as the link content. captureDiffers: the live HTML is identical (same div, data-is-link, figure, aria-hidden img and figcaption), and the empty name is how Chromium itself computes this markup, not a collector artefact. elementFails: Chromium leaves figure out of name-from-content recursion, so on Chrome and Edge the name property is empty; but AccName 1.2 (Recursive Name From Content) and HTML-AAM (figure named by its figcaption) give the name "Conheça a história da Emily", an axe-style computation finds it, and screen readers in browse mode read the caption. Whether this is a 4.1.2 failure of the content or a user-agent deviation from the spec is a point competent auditors split on, so the label is uncertain. The element clearly fails 2.1.1 (a mouse-only link with no keyboard access), which is another criterion.
